dimensions.assessment: Affects members of the Armed Forces, former service members, civilian Department of Defense employees, and veterans who served at specified facilities or the Nevada Test and Training Range.
dimensions.evidence: Members of the Armed Forces and civilian employees of the Department of Defense who are or have been stationed or employed at a covered facility

dimensions.assessment: Substantially alters disability compensation eligibility and establishes legal presumptions of toxic exposure and service-connection for specific medical conditions including lipomas and tumor-related conditions.
dimensions.evidence: Only in the case of a covered veteran described in section 1119(c)(1)(A), lipomas and tumor related conditions.

dimensions.assessment: Expands eligibility for disability compensation and veterans' benefits, which implies increased federal spending through the Department of Veterans Affairs and Department of Defense.
Amends title 38 of the United States Code and directs administrative recordkeeping expansions across the Department of Defense and Department of Veterans Affairs.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary of Defense shall expand the Individual Longitudinal Exposure Record... to document all toxic exposures

dimensions.assessment: Provides permanent statutory presumptions and ongoing recordkeeping mandates affecting current and future veteran benefit determinations.

importance_detail.rationale: The bill expands Department of Defense exposure recordkeeping, establishes toxic exposure presumptions for Department of Energy facility workers, classifies the Nevada Test and Training Range as a contaminated location, and mandates service-connection presumptions for certain conditions and radiation-risk activities.

summary: The Fighting for the Overlooked Recognition of Groups Operating in Toxic Test Environments in Nevada (FORGOTTEN) Veterans Act of 2025 requires the Department of Defense to improve documentation of military toxic exposures and establishes various presumptions of toxic exposure and service-connected disability benefits for individuals who served at the Nevada Test and Training Range and certain energy facilities.

affected_groups.effect: Have their toxic exposures and medical information tracked more comprehensively in the Individual Longitudinal Exposure Record and service records, and receive presumptions of exposure and service-connection for specific locations and conditions.
Presumed to have been exposed to toxic substances if stationed or employed at a covered Department of Energy facility.
affected_groups.group: Civilian Employees of the Department of Defense

affected_groups.effect: Receive presumptions of toxic exposure, radiation-risk activity classification for onsite participation, and service-connection presumptions for conditions including lipomas and tumor-related conditions.
affected_groups.group: Veterans who served at the Nevada Test and Training Range

affected_groups.effect: Required to expand record-keeping, identification processes, and make exposure records available to health care providers, researchers, and benefits specialists.
affected_groups.group: Department of Defense and Department of Veterans Affairs Personnel

key_provisions: Expands the Individual Longitudinal Exposure Record (ILER) to include all-hazard occupational data, environmental hazards, and medical encounter information related to toxic exposures.
Requires the Department of Defense to document in service records whether a member served at a location with potential toxic exposure, using a check box for classified locations.

Establishes a presumption of toxic exposure for Armed Forces members and civilian DOD employees stationed or employed at Department of Energy facilities covered under the Energy Employees Occupational Illness Compensation Program Act of 2000.

Requires the Department of Defense to classify the Nevada Test and Training Range (NTTR) as a location where contamination occurred, and requires the Department of the Air Force to identify individuals stationed there since January 27, 1951.
Establishes that onsite participation at NTTR locations with potential toxic exposure on or after January 27, 1951, is a radiation-risk activity.
Establishes a presumption of toxic exposure for veterans who performed active service at NTTR locations with potential toxic exposure, including the airspace above.
Adds lipomas and tumor-related conditions as service-connected conditions for covered veterans who served at NTTR locations.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Fighting for the Overlooked Recognition of Groups Operating in Toxic Test Environments in Nevada (FORGOTTEN) Veterans Act of 2025 requires the Department of Defense to improve documentation of military toxic exposures and establishes various presumptions of toxic exposure and service-connected disability benefits for individuals who served at the Nevada Test and Training Range and certain energy facilities.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters record-keeping systems and disability compensation rules for military personnel and civilian workers exposed to toxins at specific sites, most notably the Nevada Test and Training Range and Department of Energy facilities. It changes how the Department of Defense documents toxic exposures and how the Department of Veterans Affairs evaluates certain claims by establishing statutory presumptions of exposure and service connection.
